record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Quantum Information Theory
record.context_brief: Algorithmic complexity of preparing product states
record.original_question: For an m-qubit pure state psi, study the asymptotic algorithmic gate complexity of preparing n copies |psi>|psi>... as a function of n and of the gate complexity of preparing one copy of |psi> from |0>. Using a gate set such as Pauli-product rotations with cost |phi|, can the n-copy preparation ever be asymptotically more efficient, for example by cloning a known state, than repeated independent preparation?

evidence.quote: What can be said about the algorithmic complexity of preparing |ψi|ψi. . . (n times), asymptotically, as a function of n and the algorithmic complexity of preparing |ψi?
By algorithmc complexity I mean the number of gates required to prepare the state from |0i. This depends on the gate set used so the question concerns asymptotics.
It may be possible to clone |ψi more efficiently than to prepare it, given that one knows |ψi.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix a universal gate set for quantum circuits acting on qubits; for definiteness, take the gate set to consist of all single-qubit Pauli-product rotations together with CNOT, and assign unit cost to each gate (so that the gate complexity C(|\phi\rangle) of a pure state |\phi\rangle on a finite number of qubits is the minimum number of gates needed to prepare |\phi\rangle exactly, or to within a fixed accuracy \varepsilon, from the all-zeros state |0\cdots 0\rangle).

Let |\psi\rangle be an m-qubit pure state with gate complexity C(|\psi\rangle) = c. For each positive integer n, let C_n(|\psi\rangle) denote the gate complexity of preparing the nm-qubit tensor product state |\psi\rangle^{\otimes n} from |0\cdots 0\rangle.

Trivially C_n(|\psi\rangle) \le n \cdot c by preparing n independent copies. The questions are:

(1) Determine the asymptotic behavior of C_n(|\psi\rangle) as a function of n and c. In particular, characterize the function f(n,c) := \sup_{|\psi\rangle:\, C(|\psi\rangle)=c} C_n(|\psi\rangle) and the corresponding infimum / typical behavior.

(2) Does there exist an m-qubit pure state |\psi\rangle (with m possibly depending on n) and an integer n \ge 2 such that C_n(|\psi\rangle) = o(n \cdot C(|\psi\rangle)) as n \to \infty, i.e. for which preparing n copies is asymptotically strictly more efficient than n independent preparations? Equivalently, is there a known classical description of a state |\psi\rangle from which one can ``clone'' additional copies more cheaply than re-preparing them from scratch?

Provide either upper bounds showing such savings are possible, or lower bounds showing that C_n(|\psi\rangle) = \Theta(n \cdot C(|\psi\rangle)) for all families of states.
artifact.status_search_result: No specific resolution of this asymptotic gate-complexity question for n-copy preparation versus single-copy preparation was located. The question appears to remain open in the form posed; related work on state preparation complexity (e.g., lower bounds via counting arguments, Sun et al. on circuit depth for state preparation) addresses single-copy complexity but does not, to our knowledge, settle the multi-copy speedup question.
